title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 6: the vision of the Lord on his throne, the seraphim, the live coal, and "Here I am. Send me!"

questions.text: In the year of which king's death did Isaiah see the Lord on a throne?
questions.explanation: Isaiah says, "In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up."

questions.text: What did the Lord's train fill?
questions.explanation: The Lord was sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.

questions.text: How many wings did each of the seraphim have?
questions.explanation: Each seraphim had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.

questions.text: What did the seraphim call to one another?
questions.explanation: One called to another, "Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!"

answers.text: "Great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised!"
"Blessed is he who comes in Yahweh's name!"
"Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies!"

questions.text: With what was the house filled when the voice called?
questions.explanation: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.

questions.text: Why did Isaiah cry out "Woe is me!"?
questions.explanation: Isaiah said he was undone because he was a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips, and his eyes had seen the King, Yahweh of Armies.

answers.text: Because he was a man of unclean lips
Because the people had rejected him

questions.text: What did one of the seraphim bring to Isaiah?
questions.explanation: One of the seraphim flew to him with a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

answers.text: A scroll with writing on it
A measuring line in his hand
A live coal from the altar

questions.text: What did Isaiah answer when the Lord asked, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?"
questions.explanation: Isaiah answered, "Here I am. Send me!"

questions.text: When Isaiah asked "Lord, how long?", what was the answer?
questions.explanation: The Lord answered, "Until cities are waste without inhabitant, houses without man, the land becomes utterly waste."

answers.text: Until cities are waste without inhabitant
Until the people turn and repent
Until a new king is crowned

questions.text: What does the last verse say about the tenth that is left in the land?
questions.explanation: If there is a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed, like a terebinth or an oak whose stump remains when cut down; the holy seed is its stock.

answers.text: It will in turn be consumed
